title: Experimental Realization Of Qubit-state-controlled Directional Edge States In Waveguide Qed
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 03 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of qubit-state-controlled directional edge states in a waveguide QED system, enabling on-chip routing of quantum information.
motivation: To realize controllable directional propagation of photons in waveguide QED, which is essential for quantum networks and information processing.
method: Using a superconducting qubit coupled to a photonic waveguide with engineered chiral coupling, the direction of edge states is controlled by the qubit state.
result: Qubit-state-dependent directional emission and absorption of photons are observed, demonstrating a building block for quantum routers.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable approach to quantum routing and non-reciprocal devices in waveguide QED, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Two-voter Quantum Anonymous Voting Prototype With Continuous Variables
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a two-voter quantum anonymous voting protocol using continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Anonymous voting is a key multi-party cryptographic task; quantum protocols can provide information-theoretic security beyond classical means.
method: The authors implement a continuous-variable quantum anonymous voting scheme with two voters, using squeezed states and homodyne detection to ensure anonymity and verifiability.
result: The prototype successfully demonstrates anonymous voting with high fidelity and security against eavesdropping, validating the feasibility of continuous-variable quantum network protocols.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum anonymous voting is experimentally viable and could be scaled to more voters, contributing to practical quantum network applications.

title: Lieb–Liniger Interaction Via Self-interacting Stationary Light Polaritons
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to realize the Lieb-Liniger model using self-interacting stationary light polaritons in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To simulate strongly correlated quantum systems like the Lieb-Liniger model in a controlled platform, leveraging hybrid quantum systems for quantum simulation.
method: The authors design a setup where stationary light polaritons, formed by coupling light to atomic ensembles, acquire effective interactions via a nonlinear medium, mapping to the Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian.
result: They demonstrate that the system can reproduce the Lieb-Liniger model's physics, including bound states and correlation functions, with tunable interaction strength.
conclusion: This work provides a viable route to quantum simulation of integrable models using hybrid quantum systems, bridging quantum optics and condensed matter physics.

title: Quantum Metrology Based On Superconducting Qubits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper explores quantum metrology using superconducting qubits, focusing on parameter estimation and sensitivity bounds.
motivation: Quantum metrology aims to achieve precision beyond classical limits; superconducting qubits offer a promising platform due to their controllability and coherence.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate quantum metrology protocols using superconducting qubits, including Ramsey interferometry and optimal control techniques.
result: They achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation and demonstrate enhanced sensitivity over classical approaches.
conclusion: Superconducting qubits are a viable platform for practical quantum metrology, with potential applications in sensing and fundamental physics.

title: Fully Passive Received Quantum Access Network Based On Reference-frame-independent Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: A fully passive received quantum access network based on reference-frame-independent QKD is proposed and demonstrated.
motivation: To reduce the cost and complexity of quantum access networks by eliminating active components at the receiver side and to overcome the challenge of reference frame alignment.
method: The authors design a passive receiver architecture that uses a reference-frame-independent QKD protocol, enabling stable key distribution without active alignment.
result: The scheme achieves high key rates and stable performance over a passive optical network, demonstrating feasibility for practical quantum access networks.
conclusion: The proposed fully passive received quantum access network is a promising solution for scalable and cost-effective quantum communication.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with the ITU channel grid, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require multiple wavelength channels for efficient entanglement distribution, but existing sources lack integration and compatibility with standard telecom grids.
method: The authors fabricate a chip-scale source using nonlinear photonics to generate photon pairs at multiple ITU-grid wavelengths simultaneously, with characterization of brightness, purity, and indistinguishability.
result: The source achieves high brightness and low noise across multiple channels, with photon pairs showing high spectral purity and indistinguishability suitable for quantum networking protocols.
conclusion: This integrated multi-wavelength source is a practical building block for future quantum networks, enabling wavelength multiplexing and compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.

title: Constant Runtime Error Mitigation Via Restricted Evolution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a constant-time error mitigation technique for quantum circuits by restricting the evolution to a subspace that is resilient to certain errors.
motivation: Error mitigation is crucial for near-term quantum devices, but existing methods often require many circuit repetitions or post-processing. A constant-time approach could significantly reduce overhead.
method: The method restricts the quantum evolution to a carefully chosen subspace of the Hilbert space where errors are suppressed or have a known structure, allowing for efficient mitigation without iterative procedures.
result: Demonstrates that the restricted evolution approach achieves error mitigation with constant runtime overhead, independent of circuit depth, and shows improved fidelity on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical and scalable error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum computers, particularly useful for deep circuits where other methods become costly.

title: Distributed Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm On A Quantum-centric Supercomputing Architecture
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a distributed implementation of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on a quantum-centric supercomputing architecture, focusing on scalability and resource management.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of current quantum hardware by distributing QAOA across multiple quantum processors, enabling the solution of larger optimization problems.
method: The authors propose a distributed QAOA framework that partitions the problem graph, executes subproblems on separate quantum processors, and coordinates via classical communication, using a quantum-centric supercomputing architecture.
result: They demonstrate improved scalability and resource efficiency compared to monolithic QAOA, with numerical simulations showing successful optimization for graph sizes beyond single-device capacity.
conclusion: Distributed QAOA is a viable approach for near-term quantum advantage in combinatorial optimization, leveraging distributed quantum computing resources.

title: Superconductivity On Two Surfaces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Superconductivity observed in rhombohedral multilayer graphene with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
motivation: To explore unconventional superconductivity in a two-surface system within graphene.
method: Experimental study of rhombohedral multilayer graphene, measuring transport properties.
result: Superconductivity emerges from a normal state with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
conclusion: The two-surface geometry may host novel superconducting mechanisms.

title: Soft-X-ray Momentum Microscopy Of Nonlinear Magnon Interactions
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a soft-X-ray momentum microscopy technique to image nonlinear magnon interactions with nanoscale sensitivity.
motivation: Nonlinear magnon interactions are important for nanoscale spin dynamics but are difficult to detect with existing methods.
method: The authors use soft X-rays to image magnon momentum, enabling the capture of nonlinear interactions at the nanoscale.
result: The technique achieves nanometre-scale sensitivity and reveals nonlinear magnon couplings.
conclusion: Soft-X-ray momentum microscopy is a powerful new tool for studying magnon interactions and spin dynamics.

title: Superconductivity From Dual-surface Carriers In Rhombohedral Graphene
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene arising from dual-surface carriers.
motivation: To explore unconventional superconductivity in graphene-based systems with unique electronic structure.
method: Experimental transport measurements on medium-thickness rhombohedral graphene devices.
result: Multiple superconducting states are observed, attributed to wavefunctions localized on the outer layers.
conclusion: Rhombohedral graphene hosts superconductivity from dual-surface carriers, offering a new platform for studying correlated phases.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and jamming phase transitions drive tissue organization in cellular collectives.
motivation: Understanding how physical parameters like cell density and adhesion control tissue material state and organization.
method: Combines in silico simulations and in vivo experiments to independently tune cell density and adhesion.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state, and adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization.
conclusion: Phase transitions direct developmental programmes in tissues.

title: Suppression Of Coherent Light Scattering In A Three-dimensional Atomic Array
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: Experiments with a three-dimensional atomic array demonstrate strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering.
motivation: Previous studies of collective light scattering in atomic arrays focused on 1D and 2D systems; extending to 3D is important for understanding many-body light-matter interactions.
method: The authors experimentally realize a 3D atomic array and measure the suppression of coherent scattering in all directions.
result: They observe strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering, indicating collective subradiant behavior.
conclusion: 3D atomic arrays can exhibit collective optical effects not present in lower dimensions, with potential applications in quantum optics and information.

title: Watching Ionization In A New Light
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: MeV electron pulses induce strong optical transmission modulation in semiconductors, enabling room-temperature detection of ionizing radiation with sub-10-ps timing precision.
motivation: To develop next-generation medical imaging and radiation diagnostics with high temporal resolution.
method: Experimental demonstration using MeV electron pulses and optical transmission measurement in common semiconductors.
result: Observation of surprisingly strong modulation enabling sub-10-ps timing precision at room temperature.
conclusion: The findings could lead to improved medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.

title: The Thin Line For Optical Neural Networks Towards Broad Practical Relevance
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the practical challenges and research priorities for optical neural networks, focusing on their real-world applicability rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Optical neural networks promise high efficiency and bandwidth, but their practical value for general-purpose or specialized applications needs validation under realistic conditions.
method: The paper reviews recent insights and outlines key research priorities for optical neural networks, likely through analysis of existing literature and identification of gaps.
result: It identifies critical challenges such as scalability, noise, and integration that must be addressed for broad practical relevance.
conclusion: Optical neural networks require further development to meet application-realistic benchmarks before they can achieve broad practical relevance.

title: Chaotic Photonics In Microresonators
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: A review of chaotic dynamics in microresonator photonics, covering various materials and architectures.
motivation: To survey how chaos in microcavities can be harnessed for photonic technologies and fundamental science.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical work on chaotic microcavities, including ray and wave chaos, mode coupling, and nonlinear effects.
result: Chaotic photonics enables novel functionalities such as broadband light generation, sensing, and random lasing.
conclusion: Harnessing chaos in microresonators offers new opportunities for photonic devices and fundamental studies.

title: Vortices And Solitons In Polariton Superfluids And Condensates
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 14 May 2026;
tldr: A review of vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids and condensates, focusing on their formation and control for information processing.
motivation: Polariton systems exhibit nonlinear phenomena like vortices and solitons that could be used for information processing, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical work on polariton vortices and solitons, discussing their properties and control.
result: It summarizes the state of the art in generating and manipulating these nonlinear states in polariton condensates.
conclusion: Polariton vortices and solitons have potential for information processing, but the paper does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Layer-number-parity-dependent Abnormal Magnetic Ordering In Few-layer CrI3 On N-face AlN Substrate
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports layer-number-parity-dependent magnetic multistates in few-layer CrI3 on N-face AlN substrate, attributed to interfacial hole doping.
motivation: To understand how substrate interactions affect magnetic ordering in two-dimensional magnets, which is important for spintronic applications.
method: Experimental measurements of magnetic states in CrI3 flakes on N-face AlN substrate combined with first-principles calculations.
result: 5L-CrI3/AlN exhibits distinct magnetic multistates (+5 → –1 → +1 → –5) depending on layer parity, explained by hole doping from the substrate.
conclusion: The N-face AlN substrate induces a novel magnetic behavior in CrI3, highlighting the role of interfacial doping in controlling magnetism.

title: Spontaneous Photoblinking Upconversion Microscopy
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a super-resolution imaging technique using photoblinking in upconversion nanoparticles, achieving 30 nm resolution in biological cells.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy for biological imaging without requiring high laser power or complex setups.
method: They exploit spontaneous photoblinking in Yb3+/Ho3+-codoped upconversion nanoparticles under near-infrared excitation, using stochastic switching for localization-based super-resolution.
result: Achieved spatial resolution down to 30 nm at excitation power densities of about 6 kW cm−2, demonstrated in biological cells.
conclusion: This approach provides a simple, low-power super-resolution imaging method suitable for biological applications.

title: Is Ball Lightning A Relativistic Soliton?
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes that ball lightning may be explained by relativistic solitons, supported by laser experiments producing millimeter-scale solitons.
motivation: Ball lightning is a poorly understood atmospheric phenomenon; the paper aims to test whether relativistic solitons can account for its properties.
method: High-power laser experiments are used to generate relativistic solitons in a laboratory setting, and their characteristics are compared to ball lightning observations.
result: Millimeter-scale relativistic solitons are produced, suggesting that such structures could indeed be responsible for ball lightning.
conclusion: Relativistic solitons are a plausible explanation for ball lightning, warranting further investigation.

title: Implosion Carving Shrinks 3D-printed Nanostructures
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: A nanofabrication technique using hydrogel swelling and controlled shrinkage to create high-refractive-index-contrast 3D photonic nanostructures for visible light.
motivation: To overcome limitations in fabricating nanoscale 3D photonic structures with high refractive index contrast for visible-light applications.
method: 3D printing of a swollen hydrogel followed by controlled shrinkage (implosion carving) to achieve nanometre-scale features.
result: Demonstrated fabrication of high-refractive-index-contrast 3D photonic nanostructures suitable for visible light.
conclusion: Implosion carving enables scalable production of complex nanophotonic structures with potential applications in optics and photonics.

title: Metasurfaces Bridge The Terahertz Gap
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: A nonlinear metasurface enables widely tunable, continuous-wave terahertz emission at room temperature, bridging the terahertz gap.
motivation: The terahertz spectral region is difficult to access with compact, room-temperature sources; a practical solution is needed for applications in imaging, spectroscopy, and communications.
method: The authors engineer a nonlinear metasurface with a carefully designed structure to achieve efficient, tunable continuous-wave terahertz generation via nonlinear optical processes.
result: The metasurface produces widely tunable terahertz radiation at room temperature, offering a compact and efficient source.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to compact terahertz sources, potentially enabling new applications in the terahertz range.

title: Time-varying Photonics Enables Polarization Control
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates dynamic polarization control using time-varying photonics in an epsilon-near-zero material.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast polarization control for photonic applications.
method: Optical pumping of an isotropic aluminium zinc oxide film near its epsilon-near-zero regime induces birefringence, dichroism, and optical activity.
result: Sub-picosecond timescale polarization control is demonstrated.
conclusion: Time-varying photonics offers a new approach for dynamic polarization manipulation.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy From Nanoscale Imaging To Holistic Exploration
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: A commentary on the evolution of atomic force microscopy from imaging to a versatile nanoscience platform.
motivation: To highlight the broad impact and versatility of atomic force microscopy beyond surface imaging.
method: Historical review and commentary on key innovations in AFM technology.
result: AFM has become a multifunctional tool for nanoscale characterization.
conclusion: AFM continues to expand its role in nanoscience and nanotechnology.

title: Scaling Matters Of Cell Fate
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a universal scaling law in DNA methylation dynamics during early embryo development, linking physical constraints to cell fate determination.
motivation: Understanding how cell differentiation is regulated is a fundamental question in developmental biology; the authors aim to uncover whether physical principles govern methylation dynamics.
method: The study analyzes methylation data from early embryos and identifies a scaling law that describes the dynamics across different species and conditions.
result: Methylation dynamics follow a universal scaling law, suggesting that physical constraints, rather than molecular specifics, shape cell fate.
conclusion: The findings imply that cell fate determination is governed by universal physical principles, which could have implications for regenerative medicine and developmental biology.

title: Evidence For The Generic Existence Of Two Local Structures In Liquid Water
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: Simulations suggest the existence of two interconvertible local structures in liquid water, supporting the two-state model of deeply undercooled water.
motivation: Understanding the structure of liquid water, especially under deeply undercooled conditions, is important for condensed matter physics and chemistry.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to analyze local structural motifs in liquid water.
result: Evidence for two distinct local structures that undergo interconvertible reactions was found, corroborating the two-state picture.
conclusion: The two-state model of liquid water is supported by simulation evidence, providing insight into water's anomalous properties.

title: Adhesion-driven Rigidity Transition Decoupled From Density-driven Jamming Triggers Epithelial Organization In Embryonic Tissues
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies adhesion-driven rigidity transitions in embryonic tissues, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding how epithelial tissues organize during morphogenesis is a key question in developmental biology.
method: The authors use experimental and theoretical approaches to decouple adhesion-driven rigidification from density-driven jamming in embryonic tissues.
result: They identify that adhesion-driven rigidification triggers epithelial organization only when uncoupled from density-driven jamming.
conclusion: Adhesion-driven rigidity transitions are a distinct mechanism for tissue organization, separate from jamming.

abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026;

title: Transparent Conducting Electrodes For Perovskite–silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026;
tldr: A review of transparent conducting electrodes for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells, focusing on optical, electrical, and interfacial losses.
motivation: Transparent conducting electrodes are a key performance and sustainability bottleneck in high-efficiency tandem solar cells.
method: The review examines how losses arise and outlines strategies for scalable, low-indium electrodes.
result: Identifies strategies to reduce indium usage and improve electrode performance.
conclusion: Scalable, low-indium electrodes are critical for next-generation tandem solar cells.

title: Transitions Of The Atlantic Ocean Circulation
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 18 May 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews the multistable dynamics of the Atlantic Ocean circulation from a dynamical systems perspective, focusing on climate physics.
motivation: Understanding instabilities in the Atlantic Ocean circulation is crucial due to their large climate impacts.
method: The authors unify results from a hierarchy of ocean-climate models using a dynamical systems viewpoint.
result: The review synthesizes knowledge on transitions and multistability of the Atlantic circulation.
conclusion: A dynamical systems approach provides a coherent framework for studying ocean circulation instabilities.

title: Cross-probing Van Der Waals Multiferroics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: A review of cross-probing techniques to identify intrinsic multiferroicity in van der Waals materials.
motivation: To overcome limitations of conventional probing methods and enable characterization of coupled magnetic and electric orders in atomically thin multiferroics.
method: Advocates for cross-probing technologies that combine multiple characterization techniques to distinguish intrinsic multiferroicity from extrinsic effects.
result: Identifies key challenges and opportunities in probing van der Waals multiferroics, emphasizing the need for advanced cross-probing approaches.
conclusion: Cross-probing techniques are essential for advancing the understanding and application of van der Waals multiferroics in low-power magnetoelectric devices.

title: Anisodine Hydrobromide Targets Matk And Prevents Delayed rtPA Thrombolysis-induced Vasogenic Cerebral Edema In Ischemic Stroke
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies a drug treatment for vasogenic cerebral edema in ischemic stroke, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Delayed rtPA thrombolysis in ischemic stroke can cause dangerous brain edema; the authors aim to find a therapeutic agent to prevent this complication.
method: The authors use a mouse model of ischemic stroke with delayed rtPA treatment and administer anisodine hydrobromide, then assess edema and investigate the molecular mechanism via the Matk-Src pathway.
result: Anisodine hydrobromide mitigates vasogenic cerebral edema by targeting the Matk-Src pathway, protecting blood-brain barrier integrity.
conclusion: Anisodine hydrobromide is a potential therapeutic candidate to prevent edema in stroke patients receiving delayed thrombolysis.

title: Genomic And Ecological Drivers Of Parallel Arid Adaptation In Tree Grapes (Vitaceae)
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the genomic basis of succulence evolution in tree grapes, focusing on long terminal repeat retrotransposons.
motivation: Succulence is a key drought-resistance trait, but its genomic basis is underexplored.
method: Comparative genomics and phylogenetic analyses of Vitaceae species.
result: Long terminal repeat retrotransposons inserted into introns may facilitate succulence evolution and genomic adaptability.
conclusion: The study provides insights into parallel arid adaptation in tree grapes.

title: Reinforcement Learning In Linear Embedding Space Unlocks Generalizable Control Across Soft Robot Configurations
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning in a Koopman embedding space to achieve generalizable control across 33 soft robot configurations.
motivation: Soft robots are difficult to control due to their high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamics, and existing methods lack generalizability across different configurations.
method: The authors propose a reinforcement learning framework that learns a shared Koopman linear embedding space from diverse robot configurations, enabling policy transfer.
result: The system demonstrates rapid adaptation to new configurations and achieves real-world skills such as carpentry and bartending tasks.
conclusion: The Koopman embedding approach provides a scalable and generalizable control solution for soft robotics.

title: Ultrastructural Diversity And Subcellular Organization Of Nigral Lewy Pathology In Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the ultrastructure of Lewy bodies in Parkinson's disease, focusing on cellular and subcellular organization.
motivation: Understanding the formation and diversity of Lewy pathology in Parkinson's disease to gain insight into disease mechanisms.
method: Electron microscopy and ultrastructural analysis of postmortem brain tissue from Parkinson's disease patients.
result: Lewy body ultrastructure differs between cell bodies and processes, with distinct fibrillar and membranous forms.
conclusion: The findings provide new insight into how Lewy structures may form in the human brain.

title: Gene Dependency-informed Inference Of Response To Targeted Cancer Therapies
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: The paper presents FORGE, a matrix factorization framework that co-models drug response and target gene essentiality to stratify tumors for targeted cancer therapy.
motivation: Understanding drug sensitivity at a mechanistic level is crucial for effective targeted cancer therapies.
method: FORGE uses matrix factorization to integrate drug response data with gene essentiality profiles, combined with mechanistic analyses.
result: The framework enables stratification of tumors for targeted therapy based on gene dependency patterns.
conclusion: FORGE provides a computational tool to infer drug response from gene essentiality, aiding personalized cancer treatment.

title: Multi-scale Structural Engineering Enables Ultra-strong And Tough Eutectogels
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the development of ultra-strong and tough eutectogels through multi-scale structural engineering.
motivation: Improving multiple mechanical properties in polymer gels is challenging; hierarchical design can regulate interactions at different scales.
method: The authors engineered gels with hierarchical structures to control interactions across scales.
result: The resulting eutectogels exhibit ultra-strong and tough mechanical properties.
conclusion: Multi-scale structural engineering is an effective strategy for enhancing mechanical performance of polymer gels.

title: Interspecies Quorum Sensing Signals Modulate Multicellular Organization And Enhance Contact-dependent Antagonism In Vibrio Cholerae
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how Vibrio cholerae uses interspecies quorum sensing signals to modulate multicellular organization and enhance contact-dependent antagonism against competing bacteria.
motivation: Understanding how pathogenic bacteria like V. cholerae form aggregates and interact with other species within a host is important for developing anti-infective strategies.
method: The authors investigate the effect of interspecies quorum sensing signals on V. cholerae aggregate dispersal and interspecies mixing, and measure killing via contact-dependent secretion systems.
result: Upon sensing signals from competing bacteria, V. cholerae disperses its aggregates, facilitating mixing and killing of competitors via its contact-dependent secretion system.
conclusion: Interspecies quorum sensing signals can modulate V. cholerae's multicellular behavior to enhance antagonism against other bacteria.
